rows.question: At what height was the mmWave radar mounted in the bathroom fall detection study?
rows.expected: 1.87 m on the wall
rows.quote: and a mmWave node (C4001 radar with ESP32-C3) mounted on the wall at1.87 mto provide unobstructed coverage of the entire area, including the shower bay.

rows.question: How many sensor readings are in the Adebesin et al. fall detection dataset, and how many are falls?
rows.expected: 18,906 readings, of which 2169 are falls
rows.answer: 18,906 sensor readings in total, with 2,169 representing fall events.
rows.quote: Of these, 2169 samples (11.5%) represent fall events, while 16,737 samples (88.5%) capture normal activities such as sitting, standing, sleeping, and various locomotion patterns across all recorded configurations.

rows.question: What is the combined PoE budget of one Route10 and one S8-PoE?
rows.expected: 100 W (Route10 40 W + S8-PoE 60 W)

rows.question: Can the Route10 power both of its PoE+ ports at the full 30 W per port at the same time?
rows.expected: No: 2 ports x 30 W = 60 W, but the Route10 PoE budget is 40 W

rows.question: Both fall detection papers use an ESP32. How does each one send its sensor data?
rows.expected: Adebesin et al.: the ESP32 sends over LoRa to a gateway; bathroom study: ESP32-C3 nodes send 2.56 s windows over Wi-Fi to a Raspberry Pi 4B
rows.answer: Adebesin et al.'s paper states that the ESP32 handles LoRa communication with the gateway.
rows.quote: In addition to managing sensor data, the ESP32 handles LoRa communication with the gateway, ensuring seamless data transmission.

rows.question: What sampling rate does each fall detection paper use for its sensor data?
rows.expected: Adebesin et al.: 20 Hz (50 ms); bathroom study: streams mapped to a common 100 Hz
rows.quote:
Piezoelectric Sensors 34
Sampling Rate 20 Hz (50 ms)

rows.question: On the Raspberry Pi 4B, how does the end-to-end latency of the radar-only model compare with the radar and vibration fusion model in the bathroom study?
rows.expected: Radar only 28.4 ms vs fusion 15.8 ms
rows.answer: The end-to-end latency of the radar-only model is 28.4 ms, which is higher than the 15.8 ms of the radar and vibration fusion model on the Raspberry Pi 4B.
rows.quote: Raspberry Pi 4B Motion-Mamba radar only 1.3 210 5.2 pre inf end 7.5 19.8 28.4 3.80 9730 35.2

rows.question: In the bathroom study, how much energy per 2.56 s window do the radar sensing node and the vibration sensing node use?
rows.expected: Radar node (ESP32-C3 + C4001) 4740 mJ; vibration node (ESP32-C3 + ADXL345) 820 mJ
rows.answer: The radar sensing node uses 4740 mJ and the vibration sensing node uses 820 mJ per 2.56s window.
rows.quote: ESP32-C3 + ADXL345 Vibration preprocessing - - - pre inf end 0.9 - 0.9 0.32 820 - ESP32-C3 + C4001 Radar front end - - - pre inf end 2.1 - 2.1 1.85 4740 -

rows.question: Adebesin et al. cite an mmWave radar fall detection accuracy in their literature review. How does it compare with the accuracy of the full model in the bathroom study?
rows.expected: 92.3% (cited mmWave radar work, ref [10]) vs 96.1% (bathroom full model)
rows.answer: The full model's accuracy is higher than the cited mmWave radar accuracy.
rows.quote: the strongest baseline [23] reaches 94.1% accuracy and 86.7% fall recall with 35.9 ms latency and 14200 mJ per window, whereas our model achieves 96.1% accuracy and 88.0% fall recall with 15.8 ms latency and 10750 mJ per window.

rows.question: Does the ESP32 have a built-in LoRa radio, and which separate LoRa module did Adebesin et al. use?
rows.expected: No: the ESP32 has 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi + Bluetooth, not LoRa; they used an RYLR896 module

rows.answer: 40° C (104° F) for Route10 with two 2 W SFP+ modules, not found for S8-PoE

rows.question: How does the ESP32's Light-sleep current compare with its Deep-sleep current (RTC timer and memory on)?

Light-sleep - 0.8 mA
